title: Preparation of inocula for experimental infection of blood with Streptococcus pneumoniae
author: Vivas-Alegre, Fernández-Natal, et al.

steps.title: Plate bacteria on blood agar
steps.instruction: Spread the entire surface of a blood agar plate with Streptococcus pneumoniae from the stock culture and incubate overnight at 37 °C. Todd‑Hewitt agar plates may be used as an alternative medium.

steps.title: Prepare buffered Todd-Hewitt broth
steps.instruction: Harvest the grown colonies and inoculate 40 mL of buffered Todd‑Hewitt broth. Prepare the broth by supplementing Todd‑Hewitt medium with 2 % yeast extract and 20 mM Tris (pKa = 8.1), adjust the pH to 7.8 with HCl, then sterilize before use.

steps.title: Incubate culture to mid-log phase
steps.instruction: Incubate the inoculated broth at 37 °C with shaking at 200 rpm for 6–10 h; bacterial viability remains high during this interval.

steps.title: Centrifuge and collect bacterial pellet
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the culture at 10,000 × g, 6 °C for 5 min under sterile conditions, discard the supernatant, and keep all subsequent steps with the pellet at ≤ 6 °C until freezing at –80 °C.

steps.title: Wash bacterial pellet twice with PBS
steps.instruction: Wash the pellet twice with cold phosphate‑buffered saline (PBS). For each wash, resuspend the pellet in cold PBS, centrifuge at 10,000 × g, 6 °C for 5 min, and discard the supernatant. (Note: washing after freezing increases variability in viable counts.)

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge at 10,000 × g, 6 °C for 5 min and discard supernatant

steps.title: Resuspend bacteria in RPMI-1640/glycerol
steps.instruction: Resuspend the washed pellet in 1,200 µL of cold RPMI‑1640 containing 15 % glycerol.

steps.title: Aliquot and freeze bacterial stock
steps.instruction: Dispense the suspension into single‑use aliquots and freeze immediately at –80 °C. The resulting stock typically exceeds 10⁹ CFU mL⁻¹. Quantify CFU one week after freezing, as bacterial death is rapid during the first days.
